book.title: Daily Mail New Cryptic Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Something in figures having impact on idle movement

indicators.note: movement suggests the letters shifting about from where they started

parts.note: the three words taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone's idle drifting is having an effect visible in the statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something in figures' sounds like a person in a painting, but it is the definition: DECIMAL POINT.
explanation.definitionFit: The dot separating whole units from fractions appears within written numbers, so it is literally a thing inside numerals.

clue.text: Respect not about to provide protection

indicators.note: not tells us the following word is to be left out of the first word

parts.note: deference is polite respect
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Showing no regard for someone is hardly a way to keep them safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Take RE out of DEFERENCE to leave DEFENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A defence is something that guards or shields against attack, which is what protection means.

clue.text: Oh my darling fruit!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the girl addressed in the chorus of the American folk song
second meaning: a small seedless mandarin orange

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an endearment exclaimed over some fruit; the chorus of the folk song runs 'Oh my darling, oh my darling, oh my darling Clementine'.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's heroine bears the name of a small sweet citrus, so one name serves both the lyric and the orange.

clue.text: Standing on hair gives support when one's lying

parts.note: a mat is something one stands on
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone is standing on a strand of hair, oddly said to be supportive.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress is the padded base of a bed, holding you up while you sleep stretched out.

clue.text: Find after a time business can be set up inside

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece sits within the other

parts.note: late means after the expected time

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means placed upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A firm discovers it can set up shop indoors after a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to discover where it is, a straightforward synonym of finding.

clue.text: Expel famous writer with no publicity

indicators.note: with no tells us something is taken away from the writer's name

parts.note: Marcel Proust, the French novelist
PR is public relations, publicity

explanation.surface: A celebrated author is thrown out because no one is promoting him.
explanation.walkthrough: PROUST without PR leaves OUST.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to drive them out or remove them from a position, the same as expelling.

clue.text: Time up in home that's most accessible

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Time is up, and the handiest place is at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearest means closest at hand, so the easiest of all to reach or get to.

clue.text: Speed up soldiers at the end of the month making peace

parts.note: a force is a body of soldiers

indicators.note: making suggests forming something new, so the following letters are rearranged
the end of points to keeping only the final letter of each of the two little words

parts.note: final letter of the word
final letter of the word
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Troops hurry along at month's end to bring about a truce.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of 'at' and 'month' supply TH, and PEACE rearranged gives EPACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To force the pace is an idiom for pushing a race or process to go faster than it otherwise would.

clue.text: Away to defeat the unconventional

parts.note: off means away, absent
to beat is to defeat

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and overcome anyone who breaks the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat describes something quirky or out of the ordinary, rather than following accepted norms.

clue.text: A mark held by accountant to be a tonic

indicators.note: held by tells us the first piece is gripped inside the second

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
a, then a scar, a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper keeps hold of a mark that is meant as a pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: CA (chartered accountant) is split around A SCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Cascara is a bark extract once sold as a medicinal tonic and laxative, so it fits a restorative remedy.

clue.text: They fly to look after people on the go

definitions.text: They fly to look after people on the go

parts.words: They fly to look after people
parts.note: surface reading: people who rush off to care for someone
setter's reading: cabin crew who travel by plane and attend to passengers in transit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly to' suggests hurrying to help; really they fly on the aircraft themselves, looking after travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabin attendants serve and care for airline passengers during a flight, literally flying while they look after them.

clue.text: Study a secret way to sanctify

parts.note: to con is to study or pore over

indicators.note: way here means a manner or arrangement, telling us to put the letters in a different order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Researching a hidden method for making something holy.
explanation.definitionFit: To consecrate is to make sacred or dedicate formally to God, as sanctifying does.

clue.text: One may be sorry to let it drop

definitions.text: One may be sorry to let it drop

parts.note: surface reading: someone regrets letting a matter rest
setter's reading: a person who is sad sheds a drop of water from the eye

explanation.walkthrough: 'Let it drop' sounds like abandoning a subject; here sorry means sad and the drop falls from the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrow makes people cry, and what falls down the cheek when they do is a single drop from the eye.

clue.text: A lute broken in splendid cover given the sugar treatment

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged letters go within the other word
cover says the second word wraps around the first

parts.note: grand means splendid

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A damaged lute gets a fine case and is sweetened up.
explanation.definitionFit: Granulated sugar is processed into small grains, so the term names what sugar undergoes in refining.

clue.text: Agreements finally adapted for putting in writing

definitions.note: a noun: a piece of writing

indicators.note: finally adapted says only the closing letters are changed around

parts.note: treaties are formal agreements between states

explanation.surface: Accords are at last revised before being written down.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the last two letters of TREATIES to get TREATISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written work dealing systematically with a subject, a piece of scholarly prose.

clue.text: Close to being a non-starter but one gets the message

indicators.note: a non-starter has no start, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: near means close to

explanation.surface: An idea that nearly failed but still got the point across.
explanation.walkthrough: NEAR loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear is the organ of hearing, the body part that receives spoken words and sounds.

clue.text: Old King removed man from seat in the underground

definitions.note: a noun here: an underground place

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, King George
Otto, King of Greece, was deposed from his throne in 1862

explanation.surface: A former monarch ousted a rival from his throne.
explanation.walkthrough: GR is the royal cipher of King George; Otto was a king who lost his throne.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small cave, a hollow place below or within rock, so underground.

clue.text: Something said that might be cutting

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a proverb or saying
second meaning: a toothed tool for cutting wood

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like a hurtful remark, continuing the idea of something said; it is a literal tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an old proverb or maxim and a toothed blade carpenters use to cut timber.

clue.text: Fight to give medico the honour of providing clothes

parts.note: a war is a fight
DR is doctor
OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, a British honour

explanation.surface: A campaign to have a doctor decorated for supplying garments.
explanation.walkthrough: An OBE is a British award given in the honours list.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe is a person's whole collection of garments, as well as the cupboard holding them.

clue.text: Making it more comfortable for East African to give voice

parts.note: E for east
A for African
to sing is to use the voice musically

explanation.surface: An East African is allowed to speak up, which puts everyone at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Easing means relieving pain or tension, lessening discomfort so that things become more bearable.

clue.text: Voice son's distress about work given to artist

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the rest
to distress is to disturb or upset, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
op. is short for opus, a work
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A singer's son is upset about a commission handed to a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Voice' looks like a verb, but it is the definition; the scrambled son splits into two parts that enclose the other pieces, and an RA is a member of the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is the highest singing voice, and also the singer who has it.

clue.text: Protection needed from wet paint?

parts.note: surface reading: a covering to keep fresh paint off you
setter's reading: wet weather puts on a layer, as paint does, so you need a garment against it

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the wordplay: the wet coating is from the sky, and the protection is an outer garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A mackintosh or waterproof jacket shields the wearer from showers, so it guards against getting drenched outdoors.

clue.text: Interior force finding it difficult to see where there are pickings

indicators.note: interior means the inside part, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the inner letters of the word
hard means difficult

explanation.surface: An internal power struggles to spot where the rich gains are.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plantation of fruit trees, a place where crops are picked at harvest.

clue.text: Retreat beyond the turf with too much drink taken

indicators.note: in a down entry beyond means coming after, so this piece goes below the other

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A hideaway past the racecourse turf where people drink too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodden can mean stupefied by alcohol, dulled and soaked through by heavy drinking.

clue.text: High-ups offered some special psalms

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is offered

parts.note: spanning the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: Senior clergy are given a selection of particular psalms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-ups' sounds like important people; it means lofty peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are a great European mountain range, high peaks that literally rise up.

clue.text: Treasure one secures for a fairy-tale girl

parts.note: gold is treasure
I is the Roman numeral one
to lock is to secure

explanation.surface: Someone locks up a hoard of riches for a storybook heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldilocks is the golden-haired child who visits the three bears' cottage in the nursery story.

clue.text: Boss an establishment of some breeding

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a raised knob or decorative nail head
second meaning: a farm where horses are bred

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' suggests a manager and 'of some breeding' suggests a posh house; really it is a raised knob and a horse farm.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a projecting knob on a surface and a place keeping stallions to breed horses.

clue.text: Do something with drug in at last being made law

definitions.note: the answer is a past participle: made law

parts.note: E is ecstasy, the drug

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the preceding small word

parts.note: final letter of the word
acted means did something

explanation.surface: Taking action after drugs have finally kicked in, while a bill passes.
explanation.walkthrough: E for ecstasy and the last letter of 'in' come before ACTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is enacted when it is passed into statute, becoming part of the law of the land.

clue.text: Boldly confront rejected features

parts.note: out means rejected, dismissed
the face is a person's features

explanation.surface: Standing up bravely to looks that others have turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: To outface someone is to stare them down or defy them with confidence.

clue.text: Topped with what makes trees look stupid

parts.note: setter's reading: having a head made of the stuff of tree trunks
surface reading: something that makes trees seem foolish

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the answer means having a head made of timber; idiomatically it means dull-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone thick-skulled or blockheaded suggests a dense head of timber, an idiom for slowness of mind.
